source.title: Into the Rabbit Hull: From Task-Relevant Concepts in DINO to Minkowski Geometry
source.authors: Thomas Fel; Bin-Xun Wang; Michael A. Lepori; Matthew Kowal; Andrew Lee; Randall Balestriero; Sonia Joseph; E. Lubana; Talia Konkle; Demba E. Ba; Martin Wattenberg

record.tranche_reason: The study measures DINOv2 representation geometry and presents a refinement of the sparse, quasi-orthogonal direction account: it reports departures from that geometry and preliminary evidence for convex, archetypal regions. It also argues that such decompositions need not be identifiable.
record.gate_note: The paper also reports task-specific concept use, depth-cue perturbations, register concepts, and positional decoding, but these do not directly test the listed claim versions. Statements about stable SAEs from prior work are cited rather than tested here. The reported evidence for the Minkowski Representation Hypothesis is described by the authors as preliminary, not proof.
record.test_reason: On DINOv2-B, the authors argue the sparse, near-orthogonal direction picture needs refining. They propose that concepts are convex regions (Minkowski sums of polytopes) and support this with token-geometry and archetypal analyses. They also give a formal non-identifiability argument that bears on whether dictionary features are canonical. The evidence is weak as a test: the authors call it preliminary and compatible, not proof. They explicitly decline to say it contradicts the linear representation hypothesis. The subject is a vision model, so the LLM-specific version V4 is not tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors find DINOv2 representations show regularities beyond a strictly sparse, quasi-orthogonal picture and propose MRH (tokens as sums of convex mixtures of archetypes). They give theoretical arguments from multi-head attention and preliminary, model-specific empirical evidence. They explicitly refrain from saying their results contradict the linear representation hypothesis, treating MRH as a working refinement.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes a pretrained vision transformer using a learned 32,000-atom SAE dictionary and additional archetypal, token-geometry, and co-activation analyses. It is not a reproduction of the toy-model method.
record.method_sensitivity: The analysis is based on DINOv2-B, the chosen SAE dictionary, probes, and datasets; the authors state that conclusions are conditional on these choices.

fits_no_version.finding: In a real ViT, the SAE dictionary is more coherent than random and Grassmannian baselines (heavier inner-product tails) and spans a lower effective rank. Task-relevant atoms are more mutually aligned than random subsets.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Dictionary atoms recovered from real models are near-orthogonal (Grassmannian-like), as the sparse-superposition picture predicts.

fits_no_version.finding: SAE atoms have Hoyer scores far below the neuron-aligned limit, only slightly above the Gaussian baseline. Concepts are distributed across neurons in a vision transformer.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Vision models, like LLMs, spread features across many neurons, and an SAE can recover them (V4 extended to vision).

record.problems: The authors characterize the MRH evidence as preliminary and say multiple geometric hypotheses can produce similar observations. Their study is model-specific, does not causally identify concepts or head-level tiles, and reports that the relevant decompositions are generally non-identifiable. No error bars or confidence intervals are stated for the listed empirical findings.
record.rows_left_out: Not applicable; fewer than 60 relevant rows.

untested.parts: No toy networks, no sparsity-dependent transition, no study of regular geometry in small models.
No test of capacity competition or of important features getting dedicated dimensions.
Neuron polysemanticity and its causes are not studied.
No LLM is studied. The analogous evidence in a vision transformer (distributed atoms with low Hoyer scores; SAE R2 > 88%) is recorded under fits_no_version.
SAE completeness and run-to-run stability are not measured. Instability of naive SAEs is cited from prior work, and the authors use a stabilised archetypal SAE because of it.
No direct test that particular features are irreducibly multi-dimensional. MRH is tested only in its single-tile case (Archetypal Analysis), on one model and one layer.

missing.what: Hoyer sparsity of SAE atoms against random and Gaussian baselines (distributed, not axis-aligned encoding)
Positional information compresses to a ~2D subspace in late layers. Per-image token clouds stay low-dimensional and smooth after positional components are removed.
Three dense, dataset-wide positional SAE features alongside sparse ones (partly dense regime)
Weak correlation between co-activation and atom geometry (r = 0.28, R2 = 0.08)

record.verdict_notes: I downgraded the reader's V5 and V6 'challenges' labels to limits_scope. The authors say the evidence is compatible, not proof, and that multiple hypotheses could produce the same patterns. The AA-vs-SAE comparison does not discriminate between the accounts, since both reconstruct well. The non-identifiability result is conditional on MRH. Much of the paper (Elsewhere concepts, depth cues, register concepts) is off-claim. No uncertainty estimates are given for the empirical results.

versions.untested_parts: Tests neither toy networks nor a sparsity-dependent transition or regular geometry in the specified toy-model setting.
Does not test whether neuron polysemanticity results from limited-capacity competition or whether important features receive dedicated dimensions.
Does not test neuron polysemanticity or alternative causes of it.
The subject is a vision model, DINOv2-B, not an LLM; the study does not test the stated LLM evidence.
The study does not evaluate SAE feature completeness or stability across runs. Its evidence concerns reconstruction by an alternative archetypal method and the non-uniqueness of decompositions.
The empirical evidence is preliminary and model-specific; the study does not establish that all model features are multi-dimensional regions or identify their generating factors.

rows.subject: DINOv2-B
rows.operation_detail: Compared pairwise inner products of learned dictionary atoms with random and Grassmannian baselines.
rows.measure: Distribution of pairwise atom inner products / dictionary coherence
rows.value: The SAE dictionary has heavier tails and a flatter central peak, with higher coherence than the baselines.
rows.note: The result departs from a uniformly near-orthogonal dictionary, but by itself does not determine whether the underlying features are one- or multi-dimensional.
rows.check: Measures coherence of SAE atoms against random and Grassmannian baselines. That is about quasi-orthogonality in a real vision model, not feature dimensionality (V6) or toy models (V1). Moved to fits_no_version. The text gives the Grassmannian baseline's maximum coherence (0.065897) but no SAE coherence number.

rows.subject: DINOv2-B
rows.operation_detail: Measured the singular-value spectrum of the learned dictionary.
rows.value: The SAE spectrum decays more sharply than both baselines, indicating lower effective rank and anisotropy.
rows.note: The spectrum describes dictionary-level anisotropy, not the dimensionality of individual features.
rows.check: The dictionary singular-value spectrum shows global anisotropy, not whether individual features are 1-D or multi-dimensional. Moved to fits_no_version.

rows.subject: DINOv2-B
rows.operation_detail: Inspected the tails of the learned dictionary's pairwise dot-product distribution.
rows.value: A small but significant number of pairs are nearly antipodal; examples include semantically opposed patterns.
rows.note: The authors interpret these as signed semantic axes; the finding does not resolve whether features generally have one or multiple dimensions.
rows.check: The authors read near-antipodal atom pairs as opposite poles of a single signed axis. That fits 1-D features rather than challenging them, but it does not show whether features in general are 1-D. No count or proportion is given.

rows.subject: DINOv2-B
rows.operation_detail: Compared Archetypal Analysis with an SAE for token reconstruction.
rows.value: Archetypal Analysis matches SAE performance with as few as 10 archetypes per image; Figure 17 describes its error as lower than the SAE's.
rows.note: The alternative convex archetypal representation performs comparably despite stronger constraints. The paper calls this preliminary evidence for convex coding.
rows.check: Role is a method comparison (Archetypal Analysis vs SAE reconstruction). The text says AA 'matches' the SAE; the Fig 17 caption says lower error; no numbers are reported. Equal reconstruction by two decompositions shows neither that SAE features are non-canonical (V5) nor that features are multi-dimensional (V6). The SAE itself reaches R2 > 88%, so the comparison does not discriminate between the accounts.

rows.subject: DINOv2-B
rows.operation_detail: Compared straight-line token interpolation with shortest paths on a token k-nearest-neighbor graph.
rows.measure: Distance from interpolation paths to data support
rows.value: Straight lines depart the data support quickly, whereas graph geodesics remain close throughout.
rows.note: The authors interpret this as compatible with feasible displacements following piecewise paths through convex-polytopal structure.
rows.check: Straight-line paths between tokens leave the data support while k-NN geodesics stay on it. This suggests a curved, polytope-like token set rather than a plain linear span of directions. It is qualitative only (no numbers in the text), and the authors call it compatible evidence, not proof.

source_check.correct: state=cannot_determine for V6. Straight-line interpolations quickly leave data support; graph geodesics remain close. This measures aggregate token geometry, without identifying the dimensionality of individual features.
source_check.problem: The reported geometry does not establish that one-dimensional features appear incompletely; the V6 link should be none for this measurement.

rows.subject: DINOv2-B
rows.operation_detail: Examined archetypal coefficient co-activation after clustering.
rows.measure: Block structure in archetypal coefficient co-activation
rows.value: The decomposition shows bright diagonal clusters and distinct co-activating groups rather than uniform mixing.
rows.note: The authors present this as preliminary support for block-structured convex coding.
rows.check: Block structure in the co-activation of Archetypal Analysis coefficients after clustering is shown qualitatively. It does not show the dimensionality of features, and clustering can itself produce visible blocks.

rows.subject: Minkowski decomposition of convex polytopes
rows.operation_detail: Gave a mathematical argument and rectangle example for non-identifiability of Minkowski decompositions.
rows.measure: Uniqueness of decomposition into convex summands
rows.value: The decomposition is generally non-unique; a rectangle admits uncountably many distinct three-segment decompositions and infinitely many decompositions with more segments.
rows.note: The authors say activation observations alone generally cannot uniquely recover the constituent polytopes or generating factors.
rows.check: This is a mathematical proposition, not a measurement. It is conditional on MRH holding (the authors write 'and this is an assumption'). It concerns Minkowski decompositions, not SAE features directly, so 'reversed' overstates it.

source_check.locator_found: Section 7.3, Proposition 2, lines 1229–1243; Appendix J.6, lines 2713–2781.

relationships.condition: DINOv2-B last layer, ImageNet-1k validation tokens
relationships.reason: On-support geodesics versus off-support straight lines (r5) suggest convex-region rather than purely directional structure. The authors call this preliminary and compatible evidence only.
relationships.display_finding: Paths between tokens stayed on-support along geodesics but left it along straight lines, suggesting convex-region rather than purely directional structure; the authors call this preliminary and only compatible evidence.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: DINOv2-B last layer, ImageNet-1k validation tokens
source_check.reason: r5 measures support along paths between tokens, without determining whether individual features are one-dimensional. Preliminary compatibility with convex-region geometry does not establish a condition where V6 fails or holds incompletely.

relationships.condition: Conditional on the Minkowski Representation Hypothesis (theoretical argument)
relationships.reason: r7 proves that Minkowski decompositions are generally non-unique. If MRH holds, decompositions from one layer's activations, such as SAE features, cannot be canonical. This is an argument, not a measurement.
relationships.display_finding: The paper proves that Minkowski decompositions are generally non-unique, so if the hypothesis holds, decompositions of one layer's activations such as SAE features cannot be canonical. This is an argument, not a measurement.

relation.reason: Its own geometric analyses and conditional mathematical argument bear on the claim, beyond using SAEs as an interpretability tool.

tranche.reason: The paper proposes a specific refinement of directional representations and gives a conditional non-identifiability argument relevant to canonical representation units.

source_check.notes: The supplied text is the extended v3 dated 7 May 2026. The rectangle example establishes nonuniqueness by splitting collinear generators; it does not demonstrate empirically distinct SAE dictionaries.

statements.correction: Straight-line token interpolations leave data support; graph geodesics remain close. Conditions: last-layer DINOv2-B tokens, ImageNet-1k validation, cosine distance, symmetrized k-NN graph. Evidence is preliminary and compatible with multiple geometric hypotheses. Individual-feature dimensionality remains undetermined; verdict=none for r5.
statements.problem: The observation and qualifications are accurate, but limits_scope is not justified for V6 by token-support geometry alone.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: The general Minkowski-decomposition argument and the tested DINOv2-B reconstruction setting
reader_labels.reason: The paper argues that decompositions are generally non-unique, and Archetypal Analysis matches SAE reconstruction performance with few archetypes, challenging the claim that SAE features are canonical units (r4, r7).

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.reason: Archetypal reconstruction, on-support graph paths, and block-structured coefficients are presented as preliminary evidence for convex regions and sums rather than only one-dimensional directions (r4, r5, r6).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: The dictionary is more coherent and anisotropic than the near-orthogonal baseline picture, but these measurements alone do not establish the dimensionality of individual features (r1, r2, r3).
